evidence.computation: Specialist catalogue: arithmetic or weighted mean, median, complete tied modes, range, population/sample variance and standard deviation, combinations/permutations, binomial probability, and z-score. The reply kind selects the operation; this declaration is not a per-answer interpretation proof.
assumptions: Dataset operations use finite rational observations; sample variance/deviation need at least two observations. Population and sample denominators differ.
For weighted_mean only: equally long lists, nonnegative weights with positive sum; zero individual weights allowed. Mean is sum(value times weight) / sum(weights).
Combinatorial operations use bounded natural counts; binomial probability requires a valid trial count and probability in [0,1]; z-score requires positive standard deviation.
Exact rational calculations are formatted to four decimal places; standard deviation uses a checked square-root interval.

Explicit exclusions remove every equal-valued observation and retain the order and multiplicity of all remaining observations. Unsupported modifiers are refused; weighted exclusions are not supported.
untrusted: English operation recognition and complete dataset-list parsing (commas delimit observations), exact scalar lexical adapter, and JSON framing. This catalogue does not certify interpretation.

evidence.computation: Geometry catalogue: lengths, perimeters, areas, surfaces, volumes and polygon angle sums. Explicit length units are converted exactly before the existing shape computation; output names the selected unit and its dimension. Static catalogue, not an interpretation proof.
assumptions: Supported lengths: mm, cm, m, km, international inch/foot/yard; all shape lengths positive. Requested output unit takes precedence, otherwise first explicit length unit.
Bare dimensions inherit a common unit only if explicit input units agree; a mixed-unit request with any bare dimension is refused.
Pi and roots use verified intervals rounded to six significant digits.
untrusted: English roles and units, original numeric-token span binding, output unit recognition, and JSON framing.
